title: ARWP Search Release Practices
purpose: Prevent technically healthy sites from shipping with weak or contradictory search-result identity, crawl discovery, canonical-host, snippet, favicon, localization, or deployment signals. This is a release discipline, not a ranking score.

practices.question: Which hostname is the actual public site, and is this page the hostname root?
practices.practice: Resolve the canonical production hostname before editing search identity. Google site names and Search favicons are hostname-scoped, not project-subdirectory-scoped.
verify: no project path attempts to override parent-host site identity

practices.question: If a crawler only saw the homepage, would every strong identity source name the same site?
practices.practice: Keep visible brand/home link, WebSite.name, WebSite.url, genuine alternateName, og:site_name, canonical hostname, application name and homepage title coherent. Prefer one existing WebSite node over competing identity blocks.
verify: og:site_name matches a genuine site name

practices.question: Could Google reasonably infer a different title from our other title sources?
practices.practice: Use one descriptive concise title and a distinctive primary visual heading. Reconcile title, H1/prominent heading, og:title, site name, page text and important anchor text so they do not tell conflicting stories. Do not force exact equality when page intent legitimately differs.
verify: no generic Home/Profile titles or boilerplate-heavy templates

practices.question: What text near the top would become the snippet if Google ignored our meta description?
practices.practice: Write a page-specific meta description and make the visible opening copy independently useful. Keep consent banners, utility notices and repeated chrome from becoming the strongest snippet candidate; use data-nosnippet selectively for non-essential UI when appropriate. Never hide the substantive answer behind data-nosnippet.
verify: no nosnippet or max-snippet:0 when snippets are desired
utility text does not dominate the leading extract

practices.question: Does the icon still look like our brand at search-result size, and can the crawler fetch it?
practices.practice: Use a stable, representative square favicon with a supported raster or ICO option. Keep Googlebot access to the homepage and Googlebot-Image access to the favicon. Prefer a simple mark that remains recognizable at 16–32 px; verify actual bytes and dimensions rather than trusting HTML declarations.
verify: at least 8x8 and preferably larger than 48x48

practices.question: Do canonical, redirects, sitemap, structured data, social URLs and internal links all vote for the same public hostname?
practices.practice: Choose one canonical host and keep canonical links, WebSite/WebPage URLs, og:url, sitemap URLs and internal absolute links aligned. Treat HTTP/HTTPS, www/non-www, default github.io and custom-domain variants as duplicate-host candidates that need a coherent redirect/canonical policy.
verify: one valid head canonical per HTML page
no old-host URLs in current sitemap
internal links prefer final canonical URLs

practices.question: Can the same homepage be reached under multiple protocol or host variants?
practices.practice: Inspect HTTP/HTTPS, www/non-www and legacy/default-host homepage variants. Redirect duplicates to the chosen host where the platform supports it and keep site-name identity consistent on accessible duplicates until consolidation is complete.
verify: redirect targets are final canonical root
site identity does not conflict across reachable duplicates

practices.question: Is GitHub Pages serving the exact domain contract we think it is?
practices.practice: For GitHub Pages custom domains, verify the domain before use, configure supported DNS, enable HTTPS enforcement, avoid wildcard DNS, and configure the apex/www pair so GitHub can redirect the non-canonical variant to the chosen domain.
verify: DNS points to documented GitHub Pages targets

practices.question: Does the sitemap describe the site we want indexed, or the site our build happened to emit?
practices.practice: Publish a root sitemap containing current canonical indexable URLs only. Remove deleted, redirected, noindex and old-host URLs. Use lastmod only when it reflects meaningful page changes rather than build time.
verify: canonical root is represented when indexable

practices.question: Can crawlers reach the pages and assets we are asking them to understand?
practices.practice: Keep intended public roots and priority paths crawlable, distinguish crawl policy from noindex, and expose the canonical sitemap through an absolute Sitemap directive in robots.txt. Evaluate Googlebot, Googlebot-Image, Bingbot and OAI-SearchBot according to publisher policy.
verify: favicon asset not blocked for Googlebot-Image
OAI-SearchBot policy reviewed separately from GPTBot

practices.question: Can a crawler and a person reach every important page through meaningful links without knowing the URL?
practices.practice: Use crawlable a[href] links and descriptive anchor text. Ensure important canonical pages have at least one useful internal discovery path, preferably contextual or hub-based rather than footer-only link inflation.
verify: important pages have inbound internal paths
redirecting aliases are not the dominant link targets

practices.question: Does every localized page point to itself and the same alternate set, on the canonical host?
practices.practice: Use fully qualified reciprocal hreflang links, including self references. Add x-default where it represents the appropriate fallback. Keep canonical and hreflang roles distinct and do not combine unrelated alternate semantics in one link tag.
verify: one hreflang relation per link tag

practices.question: Is the hostname root a real search identity surface or just a thin launcher?
practices.practice: When the root is a language selector or gateway, keep enough stable brand/purpose text and the canonical WebSite identity at the hostname root. If a locale page is the true destination, use an explicit, crawlable routing strategy without creating a contradictory root identity or a thin indexable doorway.
verify: root has clear brand and purpose

practices.question: Are we checking the bytes that will actually ship, after every generator and post-processor?
practices.practice: Run search identity, canonical, sitemap, robots and localization checks against the final generated artifact after all render/post-processing steps. Then verify the deployed production revision separately. Source templates or a green earlier stage are not release evidence.
verify: generated metadata inspected after last post-processor
deployment did not restore stale metadata

practices.question: After a real change, how do engines learn about the changed canonical URLs?
practices.practice: Keep Search Console/Bing sitemap submissions healthy and use IndexNow for participating engines when appropriate. Submit only real added, updated or deleted canonical URLs; notification is not indexing proof.
verify: IndexNow key/host scope valid when used

practices.question: What old URLs or hostnames still carry links, crawl history or user bookmarks?
practices.practice: For moves, map old URLs to corresponding new canonical URLs, use permanent server redirects where available, update canonicals/hreflang/internal links/sitemaps, and keep redirects for a long transition. A canonical tag is not a substitute for a proper move redirect.
verify: permanent redirects work where platform permits

practices.question: Are several sites accidentally presenting the same publisher boilerplate instead of distinct product identities?
practices.practice: Reuse the release checklist, not the brand copy. Each hostname needs its own real site name, homepage promise, title, description, favicon and semantic identity. Avoid copy-pasted descriptions and generic hosting identity across a portfolio.
verify: site names are distinct where products are distinct
no cross-host canonical or structured-data leakage

practices.question: What did the search engine actually select after recrawl?
practices.practice: After deployment, inspect Search Console URL Inspection and real Search appearance for site name, title, snippet, favicon and selected canonical. Record the observation date and query/context. Repository state cannot prove the displayed result.
verify: site name/title/snippet/favicon observed after processing window
Bing URL inspection or index state reviewed when relevant
differences become new evidence, not assumptions
